regions.text: Lexington and Concord. So it was a
regions.explanation: From 53.60s to 57.62s (“Lexington and Concord. So it was a”), the share of energy above 2 kHz dropped to 5.0% from 7.4% (-32%); that is 1.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Energy above 2 kHz carries consonant bursts and fricatives (t, k, s, f); losing it blurs word boundaries and makes the speech sound muffled even at normal volume. Fix: Open the mouth more and finish final consonants crisply.
